title: React Styling Applied Check
description: Apply React styling knowledge to conditional classes, CSS Module scope, styled-components props, Tailwind composition, Bootstrap usage, dark mode, responsive design, and accessibility edge cases.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A component imports `styles from './Card.module.css'` but renders `<div className="card">`. What is the likely issue?

options.text: The local module class is not used; it should usually be `className={styles.card}`
CSS Modules require inline styles only
The component must be a class component

questions.explanation: CSS Module class names are exposed through the imported object. A plain string targets a global class, not the generated local class.

questions.prompt: Which conditional CSS Module expression is safest for an active tab?
questions.explanation: The base class should remain present, and the active class can be appended conditionally.

questions.prompt: A styled button uses `${props => props.primary && 'color: white;'}`. What mistake should you avoid?

options.text: Forwarding styling-only props to the DOM when they are not valid attributes

questions.explanation: Styling-only props can leak invalid attributes to DOM elements. Many teams use transient props or wrapper components to avoid this.

questions.prompt: Which Tailwind class patterns are valid for responsive or state styling? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Tailwind uses variant prefixes for breakpoints and states. Raw CSS media queries do not belong directly in a className string.

questions.prompt: A dark theme reads `localStorage.theme` during the first render and the page flashes from light to dark. What should you consider?

options.text: Initialize theme as early as possible and use CSS variables or a root class to avoid theme flash
Use color alone to show validation errors
Wait until the user clicks twice

questions.explanation: Theme flash happens when the initial paint uses one theme and React later switches it. Early root theme setup and CSS variables help.

questions.prompt: Using Bootstrap classes in React means you can ignore semantic HTML and ARIA concerns.
questions.explanation: Bootstrap provides styles and components, but accessibility still depends on semantic markup, labels, roles, focus behavior, and correct usage.

questions.prompt: A responsive card grid looks good visually but keyboard users cannot see which card action is focused. What is the styling problem?
questions.explanation: Keyboard users need clear focus indication. Removing outlines without replacement is a common accessibility mistake.

questions.prompt: Which choice best handles a dynamic width based on runtime data, such as progress percent?

options.text: Use an inline style for the numeric dynamic value and classes for the rest
Generate arbitrary global CSS files on every render
Use a random class name every render

questions.explanation: Inline styles are reasonable for truly dynamic values, while classes can continue to handle reusable visual rules.
